label: Product strategy
headline: A first release should answer one question for one person.
body: How we scope an MVP so one real user can test it.
voice: A first release should answer one question for one person. Here is how we scope an MVP so one real user can test it.

label: Product strategy
headline: Use a scope ladder.
body: Cut scope without cutting the product's reason to exist.

steps.title: Decision minimum
steps.text: The smallest path that produces a useful answer or output.

steps.title: Trust minimum
steps.text: Sources, limits, error states and feedback required for someone to rely on it.

steps.title: Learning minimum
steps.text: Events and prompts required to understand what happened after launch.

voice: Use a scope ladder. First, the decision minimum: the smallest path that gives a useful answer. Then the trust minimum: sources, limits and feedback, so someone can rely on it. Then the learning minimum: the events you need to understand what happened after launch.

label: Product strategy
headline: Write the test before the build.
body: Who will use it, what they will try to do, what result counts as success, and what you will measure to see it.
